A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DAS research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support comparison, including matching the renumbered appendices and figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic-distribution experiments and text-to-image evaluations covering single rewards, multiple rewards, online optimization, SDXL, and JPEG compressibility.

after.justification: v2 retains those original empirical results and adds a test-time compute-scaling experiment in Appendix E and Figure 8.

M1.justification: DAS retains the same tempered intermediate distributions, guided proposal, weighting, resampling, and online adaptation. Section 3 and Appendix A show no substantive algorithm change; the newly evaluated simplified SMC is a comparator.

E1.justification: The synthetic distributions, image-generation datasets, reward tasks, and online scenarios are retained. Appendix E varies computational budgets within the existing image reward-alignment task without introducing a new documented dataset, domain, or task requirement.

E2.justification: The new scaling comparison evaluates Best-of-N and SMC using pretrained transitions without either tempering or the guided proposal. This SMC comparator differs from the earlier no-tempering ablation. Existing comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Appendix E adds a protocol sweeping 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, and 128 particles and plotting PickScore and HPSv2 against inference compute in TFLOPs. This supplements the earlier particle-count tempering ablation; previously reported evaluation settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: The new study examines reward performance as inference compute increases and jointly compares DAS's proposal and tempering against omitting both. The existing tempering, manifold-deviation, and initialization/parameterization analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Existing Figure 2 error bars are unchanged. The added scaling curves introduce no error bars, repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: New Figure 8 reports PickScore and HPSv2 compute curves showing DAS above Best-of-N and the simplified SMC across overlapping plotted budgets. These are additional results; Tables 1–4 and the previously reported plots and qualitative samples are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation, propositions, assumptions, derivations, and proofs remain substantively unchanged, including Appendices B–C and the relocated diffusion-sampler analysis. Edits to notation punctuation and explanatory wording do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of training-free reward alignment, preserved diversity/generalization, and sample-efficient tempered SMC. Emphasizing 'test-time' restates the existing method's operating regime without changing the core contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix E explicitly acknowledges additional inference computation and interprets the new comparisons as evidence that DAS's proposal and tempering improve compute efficiency. Existing explanations of over-optimization, applicability, and future extensions remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix E documents the exact particle-count grid and construction of the added baselines, including final reward selection for Best-of-N and pretrained proposals for SMC. Existing implementation details, pseudocode, and code-access statements are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds limited positioning around inference-time scaling and Best-of-N, citing works such as Beirami et al., Khanov et al., Snell et al., and Ma et al., plus Del Moral et al. for SMC. The main related-work discussion and novelty positioning are otherwise retained.

P1.justification: The title changes to 'Test-Time Alignment of Diffusion Models Without Reward Over-Optimization,' with localized introductory and explanatory edits. A new Appendix E shifts the former Appendices E–G to F–H, while the overall narrative structure remains intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the two-panel compute-scaling Figure 8. Existing figure contents and table structures are retained, with subsequent figures renumbered, some captions edited, and surrounding text and displays reflowed.

improvement.justification: v1 supported efficiency mainly through particle-count tempering analyses; v2 adds direct reward-versus-compute comparisons against relevant inference-time alternatives in Appendix E and Figure 8. This strengthens the practical efficiency evidence while preserving earlier contributions. The gain is limited because the new study lacks uncertainty reporting and detailed FLOP-accounting information.
